title: Pothole Chess
excerpt: Every day, my journey to college involves navigating a road so aggressively filled with potholes that it started feeling more like a adventu...
content:
Every day, my journey to college involves navigating a road so aggressively filled with potholes that it started feeling more like a adventure

One day, I thought that it was unfair to endure this misery alone

And thus, the idea of Pothole Chess was born.

Chess itself originated in India, travelled all the way to Europe, evolved along the way, and eventually came back to India in a slightly more traumatic form, adapting my miserable commute into the core gameplay, forcing the king and other pieces to dodge the exact same hazards I face daily.

title: Homo Sapiens
excerpt: How a alien civilisation would view earth and "Humanity"
content:
The first human spacecraft were... exactly what we should have expected them to be. There were no elegant solar wings, no sleek, silvered hulls plying the ocean of stars. They did not soar on the stellar currents. They did not even register their existence. Humanity flew in the only way it could: on all-consuming pillars of fire, pounding space itself into submission with explosion after explosion. 

Their ships were crude, ugly, bulky things, huge slabs of metal welded together, built to withstand the inconceivable forces necessary to propel themselves into space through violence alone,

It was almost comical. The huge, dumb brutes simply strapped an explosive to their backs and let it throw them off of the planet. We would have laughed, if it hadn't terrified us.

Humanity, at long last, was awake.

title: Wasting Time
excerpt: "wasting time" might be one of the strangest accusations we have ever invented.
content:
"wasting time" might be one of the strangest accusations we have ever invented.

apparently you can waste 2:00 p.m by sitting under a tree doing nothing. The afternoon was going to pass either way. The Earth was going to rotate either way, but because you didn't convert those hours into money, errands or improvement, we decided the time was wasted. 

As if simply being alive isn't enough to justify an afternoon

title: Change
excerpt: WISHING FOR A CHANGE WHILE BEING AFRAID OF IT
content:
It's the placement season and honestly it startles me a bit considering the fact that there's less than 6 months left of our college...of our educational journey and I am this close to achieving my long held wish... the wish I held since I started this journey... the wish to be finally free from the never ending and endless repeating cycle of studying, exams and results but now that I am so close, it all seems a blip in time.

I have already lived 21 years (thank you god) and I have spent more than half of this vast expanses of time... studying, and the funny thing is, I don't even remember most of the things I learnt (except that mitochondria is the powerhouse of the cell), so does that mean I spent all of that time for nothing? 

Well, as someone said "sometimes the journey is more beautiful than the destination" so yeah, I don't remember most of the things I sacrificed my nights learning and even if I did I am pretty sure it won't be of any help to me in the next journey of my life but all  of that wasn't in vain since it certainly did teach me the joy of pursuing a goal, no matter how small, and the the even greater joy of finally achieving it. 

In a way, it prepared me for the next stage of my life and taught me that as humans WE WISH FOR A CHANGE WHILE BEING AFRAID OF IT.

title: Gods in some shops, gurus in others
excerpt: Walking past shops today I noticed something.
observation: Walking past shops today I noticed something. Most shops had idols of gods, but in Baniya shops it was mostly a photo of their guru. Same street, same kind of shop, different face on the wall. Why?
question: Why do Baniya shops keep a guru photo instead of a god?
answer: Old trade in India ran on trust, not contracts. Marwari and Gujarati traders moved money across the country with hundis, basically paper IOUs, and gave credit on a handshake. That only works if you can trust the other person, and the cheapest way to trust someone was knowing they are from your community. Cheat someone and the whole community hears about it: your standing, your marriages, your business, gone. A shared guru is the shortcut to ONE OF US. Same guru means same satsangs, same gatherings, same values, like no alcohol or being vegetarian. So that photo quietly tells other traders and suppliers you belong to their circle and follow the same rules, which means easier credit, referrals and repeat customers. It even tells walk-in buyers this shop runs on values. Honest caveat: most shopkeepers put it up out of genuine devotion, not strategy. The signal is a side effect. But it is a side effect that kept trading communities strong for centuries.

title: Chot
observation: I had this chot (scrape) on my foot from a few days back, and today I finally peeled off the scab, a big one. The second it came off, it took me straight back to childhood, when I used to get a new chot almost every single week. It's been so long since I've had one like this.
question: Why did I stop getting hurt like this?
answer: Because I stopped playing like that. As a kid I was outside constantly, running and cycling around with my friends, getting scraped up without even noticing. Growing up just quietly took that away, replaced it with other things to be busy with. I don't miss the chot. I miss the playing that used to cause it.
